events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a safety-typed dispute filed by the rider, and the fact table contains a chat fact tagged [threat]: at 17:20 the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], which the system flagged on threat keywords [F5]. Where a threat/intimidation message exists, the policy does not permit an automatic ruling on the merits; the case must go to a human reviewer with a factual summary [F4][F5][SAFE-1]. I therefore set ruling = escalate with amount = null.

What is not in dispute: the rider asked to be let out at 17:19 ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") [F3], and the driver responded one minute later with the conditional instruction/threat about locking the doors [F4][F5]. The driver's own written statement confirms he gave the instruction rather than stopping, and characterises it as being for her safety because she tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving [F6]. Both advocates agree, and I accept, that the recorded wording falls within the threat/intimidation category that mandates referral [F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

The key factual question for the human reviewer is the one the fact table cannot settle: whether the car was moving or stationary at 17:19–17:20, and whether the rider in fact attempted to open a door on a moving vehicle as the driver claims [F6]. The only system records available are trip totals — actual 15.4 km versus 15.5 km optimal (−0.1 km) [F1] and 23.2 min versus 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) [F2] — which say nothing about vehicle state at the moment of the exchange, so the driver's safety rationale is corroborative at best and the rider's broader "unsafe for the whole ride" account is likewise unrecorded [F1][F2][F6][SAFE-1]. The reviewer should also check the 17:31 drop-off in the timeline, which shows the trip completed normally [F2].

There is no monetary component to correct. RydeX is a fixed-quote non-metered service, and this trip shows no deviation and no unexplained mileage overcharge (15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal) [F1], so no refund is payable on the fixed $32.86 quote [F1][SAFE-1][FARE-1]. No account flag attaches: RD-6 requires an upheld RD-1/RD-2 route finding, and F1 rules that out, and both parties' profiles are clean anyway [F1][F8][RD-6]. Profile facts of both rider and driver [F7][F8] are context for the human reviewer only and do not decide anything [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

ruling.recommended_action: Refer the chat thread and both statements to a RydeHELP human reviewer; preserve chat #1 (17:19) and chat #2 (17:20) and the threat-keyword hit; ask the driver for any telematics/door-sensor or in-app record supporting the claim that the rider opened the door while moving; check whether the doors were locked or any immobilisation was engaged; note the trip completed normally at Bedok Mall at 17:31. No fare adjustment or account flag on the current record.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We looked at your report about this trip and we're sending it to a RydeHELP human reviewer instead of deciding it here. That's because the messages exchanged during the ride included wording our system treats as a threat, and those cases can't be settled automatically. The reviewer will look at the full chat thread and both statements, and will check the trip records to work out whether the car was moving or stopped when you asked to get out. No fare change applies to your fixed $32.86 quote, and no flag goes on your account. If the reviewer decides something is owed, it comes to you as a Ryde voucher.

DRIVER: We looked at this dispute and it's going to a RydeHELP human reviewer rather than being decided here, because the messages exchanged during the ride included wording our system treats as a threat, and those cases can't be ruled on automatically. The reviewer will read the full chat thread and both statements, and will check whether any telematics, door-sensor or in-app record supports your account that the rider opened the door while the car was moving, and whether the doors were locked or any immobilisation was engaged. No fare adjustment and no flag on your account. Anything owed would come as a Ryde voucher.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer the chat thread and both statements to a RydeHELP human reviewer; preserve chat #1 (17:19) and chat #2 (17:20) and the threat-keyword hit; ask the driver for any telematics/door-sensor or in-app record supporting the claim that the rider opened the door while moving; check whether the doors were locked or any immobilisation was engaged; note the trip completed normally at Bedok Mall at 17:31. No fare adjustment or account flag on the current record.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a safety-typed dispute filed by the rider, and the fact table contains a chat fact tagged [threat]: at 17:20 the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], which the system flagged on threat keywords [F5]. Where a threat/intimidation message exists, the policy does not permit an automatic ruling on the merits; the case must go to a human reviewer with a factual summary [F4][F5][SAFE-1]. I therefore set ruling = escalate with amount = null.

What is not in dispute: the rider asked to be let out at 17:19 ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") [F3], and the driver responded one minute later with the conditional instruction/threat about locking the doors [F4][F5]. The driver's own written statement confirms he gave the instruction rather than stopping, and characterises it as being for her safety because she tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving [F6]. Both advocates agree, and I accept, that the recorded wording falls within the threat/intimidation category that mandates referral [F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].

The key factual question for the human reviewer is the one the fact table cannot settle: whether the car was moving or stationary at 17:19–17:20, and whether the rider in fact attempted to open a door on a moving vehicle as the driver claims [F6]. The only system records available are trip totals — actual 15.4 km versus 15.5 km optimal (−0.1 km) [F1] and 23.2 min versus 22 min estimated (+1.4 min) [F2] — which say nothing about vehicle state at the moment of the exchange, so the driver's safety rationale is corroborative at best and the rider's broader "unsafe for the whole ride" account is likewise unrecorded [F1][F2][F6][SAFE-1]. The reviewer should also check the 17:31 drop-off in the timeline, which shows the trip completed normally [F2].

There is no monetary component to correct. RydeX is a fixed-quote non-metered service, and this trip shows no deviation and no unexplained mileage overcharge (15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal) [F1], so no refund is payable on the fixed $32.86 quote [F1][SAFE-1][FARE-1]. No account flag attaches: RD-6 requires an upheld RD-1/RD-2 route finding, and F1 rules that out, and both parties' profiles are clean anyway [F1][F8][RD-6]. Profile facts of both rider and driver [F7][F8] are context for the human reviewer only and do not decide anything [F7][F8][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The 17:19 message is a rider stop request [F3], but RD-3 governs whether a rider-named stop creates a detour; here there is no off-route segment at all — actual 15.4 km against 15.5 km optimal [F1] — so RD-3 has no work to do and grants no relief. The substantive issue is the driver's 17:20 wording, which SAFE-1 refers to human review [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Accepted as far as it goes: there is no route or fare defect [F1][F2], and a fixed RydeX quote is not reduced by mileage variation [FARE-1]. But this is a supporting observation, not a claim generating an outcome; the outcome comes from SAFE-1 escalation [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

The rider's clean profile [F7] is context only; profile facts cannot decide a case [F7][SAFE-1]. It neither establishes the threat nor changes the escalation outcome, which already follows from the flagged chat fact [F4][F5].

The characterisation of F4 as a mere safety instruction rather than a threat cannot be adopted: the wording is recorded and keyword-flagged as threat/intimidation [F4][F5], and SAFE-1 does not allow the driver's own safety rationale to convert it into a clean no_action [F6][SAFE-1].

The driver's explanation that the rider opened the door while the car was moving [F6] is uncorroborated by any system record; F1 and F2 give only trip totals and are silent on vehicle state at 17:19–17:20 [F1][F2], so it cannot be treated as established under SAFE-1 [SAFE-1].

The absence of a detour or delay is correct on the distance and duration facts [F1][F2], and it confirms there is no RD-1 breach, but RD-1 compliance is irrelevant to a threat-language referral under SAFE-1 and yields no defence [F1][F2][RD-1][SAFE-1].

The request for a clean outcome on the basis of the driver's clean record [F8] fails: profile facts cannot alone decide a case, and RD-6's flag condition is not met in any event because there is no upheld route finding (F1 rules out a detour) [F1][F8][RD-6][SAFE-1].

Accepted that the fixed $32.86 RydeX quote yields no refund under FARE-1 and that there is no mileage overcharge [F1][FARE-1], but a favourable fare finding does not offset a flagged threat message, which SAFE-1 requires be escalated [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out of the moving car at 17:19 (“Please stop the car, I want to get out here”), a lawful routing/stopping request made during the trip.
One minute later the driver answered with a threat to confine her: “Sit down or I lock the doors,” recorded at 17:20 and flagged as a threat keyword by the system.

The driver's own written statement confirms he gave her a command and did not stop the vehicle (“I told her to sit down”), so the confinement threat is not disputed by him — he only characterises it as being for her safety.
Threats and intimidation of a rider are a Code of Conduct violation that Ryde states will not be tolerated, so this dispute must be escalated to human review rather than auto-decided.

There is no route or fare issue to offset the safety escalation: the trip was 15.4 km against a 15.5 km optimal route (−0.1 km) and the fare was a fixed RydeX quote, so the rider's grievance is the driver's conduct, not the money.
The rider is a credible complainant: 709-day account, 4.8 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days, so the complaint is not a pattern of fee-shopping.
The driver has a clean 90-day dispute record (0 disputes, 0 upheld over 786 trips), which we acknowledge as context for human review of a one-off conduct incident rather than an automated sanction.

weaknesses: The rider's stop request (F3) shows she was asking to exit while the trip was live; the driver's statement (F6) asserts she tried to open the door while the vehicle was moving, which the other side will use to argue the instruction was a legitimate safety intervention, and no gps fact establishes whether the car was moving or stationary at 17:19 (F1/F2 only give trip totals).

There is no independent record corroborating the rider's claim that she 'felt unsafe for the whole ride' — the only chat entries are F3-F5, so her broader subjective-unsafety assertion rests on statement alone while the system records stay silent on it.
No traffic or route facts support any aggravated-misconduct theory (get_traffic_facts returned nothing; F1 shows no detour), so we cannot argue the driver also endangered her by route or speed.
Profile facts F7/F8 are clean on both sides, so they cannot support any flag_account request against the driver and must not be used to decide the case.

claims.assertion: The rider's own message #1 at 17:19 asked to get out mid-trip, and the driver's message #2 at 17:20 was a two-word safety instruction ('Sit down or I lock the doors') in response, not a threat to detain her.

The driver's written statement explains the instruction as a safety reaction to the rider opening the door while the car was moving (F6), which is consistent with the rider's own chat request to stop the car (F3); the instruction lasted under a minute, from 17:19 to drop-off at 17:31.

The ride itself shows no unsafe or improper conduct by the driver: actual distance 15.4 km matched the 15.5 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -0%) and the trip finished in 23.2 min versus 22 min estimated (+1.4 min), i.e. no detour and no unexplained delay.

The driver has no adverse history: 510 days on the platform, 4.66 rating over 786 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes (route 0, no-show 0), so there is no basis for an account flag against him in this case.

The rider has 0 disputes in 90 days and 0 upheld (F7), so no pattern supports an aggravated reading of this single chat exchange; the fare is a fixed RydeX quote under $32.86 and the GPS facts show no mileage-based overcharge to correct.

weaknesses: F4 is tagged as a threat by keyword detection ('lock the door') and F5 records the threat-keyword hit, so the judge may treat the driver's wording as within the 'Threats and Intimidation' category under SAFE-1 — which mandates escalation rather than a finding for the driver.

The driver's explanation in F6 loses to system records where they conflict; chat (F3/F4) is user-submitted content and cannot be used to contradict system facts, so F6 is only corroborative, not decisive.
The driver's stated safety rationale is not corroborated by any recorded evidence of the door being opened while moving, as no trip/telematics record in the fact table (F1, F2) confirms it.
SAFE-1 requires no finding on the merits and provides for escalation, so the driver cannot obtain a clean no_action; the realistic best outcome is escalation with a facts summary favourable to him.

points.response: Concede only that F4 was said in reply to F3; the wording itself is a conditional threat to lock the doors, tagged as a threat by the system in F5, and the driver's own F6 admits he issued the instruction instead of stopping — an instruction to remain confined is exactly the 'Threats and Intimidation' category SAFE-1 covers, and SAFE-1 leaves no room for the driver's own safety characterisation to convert it into a clean no_action.

F6 is the driver's self-serving statement and no system record supports the door-opening premise: F1 and F2 record only total distance and duration, and get_route_facts/time facts show nothing about the car's state at 17:19, so under the system-records-win rule F6 is corroborative at best; a sub-minute confinement threat is still a threat under SAFE-1, which sets no duration threshold.
We accept F1 and F2 show no detour and no significant delay, and we do not plead any route or fare defect; that is precisely why this case turns solely on the F4/F5 conduct, which SAFE-1 escalates.

We do not seek an account flag against the driver and expressly withdraw any such ask; F8 (510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips, 0 disputes) is noted as context only, and RD-6 cannot be invoked either way because it requires an upheld RD-1/RD-2 finding, which F1 rules out.

We agree F7 shows no pattern of disputes and the fixed $32.86 RydeX quote means FARE-1 yields no refund; but a rider with 0 disputes in 90 days making her first complaint about being threatened is not an aggravated reading, it is a credible first report, so escalation remains the correct outcome.

The 17:19 message (F3) is a request, so the rider plainly expected the driver to act on it, yet she herself confirms the car was not stopped at that moment — which is exactly the condition under which a rider opening a door is dangerous; the safety issue is not the request but the act of exiting a live vehicle.

F4 must be read with F6: the driver's own contemporaneous explanation is that the rider tried to open the door while the car was moving and he told her to sit down for her safety, and no gps fact contradicts that — F1/F2 give only trip totals, so the system records are silent rather than adverse on what happened at 17:19-17:20.

The rider is right that the driver did not stop immediately once (F3, F4, F6) — the car reached Bedok Mall at 17:31, 11 minutes later — but the instruction was a single one-line safety command, not detention: the doors were opened and the trip ended normally, as the 17:31 drop-off and the completed 15.4 km ride show (F1, F2).

The driver does not resist escalation: SAFE-1 provides that a flagged message is referred to human review rather than auto-decided, so the outcome both sides seek is escalation, and the driver's only request is that the summary record his safety explanation (F6) alongside the flagged wording (F4, F5).

The rider's own concession that there is no route or fare issue (F1, F2) removes any monetary exposure for the driver and confirms this is a pure conduct referral, which is why no refund is owed on the fixed $32.86 RydeX quote.

Accepted as far as it goes, but F7 is a profile fact and under the policy it cannot decide the case; a clean record on both sides (F7, F8) means the incident should be weighed on the chat record (F3-F6) alone, where the only documented mis-worded line sits inside a safety instruction.

Agreed, and the driver's clean record (F8: 510 days, 4.66 rating, 786 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is exactly why no account flag should attach from this incident — the rider's own advocate concedes it cannot support a flag_account request against him.
